# infrawrench_account (Resource)

A connected cloud account — the credential Infrawrench uses to list and manage one provider's resources.

This is the resource that makes onboarding an environment reproducible: a new organization gets its accounts, cost centres, budgets and alerts from one `terraform apply` instead of from a runbook.

**Credentials are write-only.** No route returns them, so the provider cannot detect drift on their values: a secret rotated in the Infrawrench UI will not show up as a diff here, and the next apply that touches `credentials` overwrites it. Feed them from a secret manager rather than a literal — and remember that whatever Terraform sends is in the state file and in any saved plan.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# Credentials are write-only: no route returns them, so the provider cannot
# detect drift on their values, and whatever Terraform sends is in the state
# file. Feed them from a secret manager rather than a literal.
resource "infrawrench_account" "production" {
  plugin_id    = "aws"
  display_name = "Production (eu-west-1)"

  credentials = {
    accessKeyId     = var.aws_access_key_id
    secretAccessKey = var.aws_secret_access_key
    region          = "eu-west-1"
  }
}

# A connection made for Costs alone: the credential only needs the billing
# permissions, the bill is read, and no resources are synced. Leave `products`
# out to use a connection for every app its plugin offers.
resource "infrawrench_account" "billing" {
  plugin_id    = "aws"
  display_name = "Billing (payer account)"
  products     = ["costs"]

  credentials = {
    accessKeyId     = var.billing_access_key_id
    secretAccessKey = var.billing_secret_access_key
    region          = "us-east-1"
  }
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `credentials` (Map of String, Sensitive) The plugin's credential fields, keyed by the field names that plugin declares — `accessKeyId` and `secretAccessKey` for AWS, a kubeconfig for Kubernetes, a personal access token for most SaaS providers. The account creation form in the app lists them per plugin.

A write replaces the whole set, so send every field the plugin needs and not just the one you are rotating.
- `display_name` (String) Name shown throughout the app, e.g. `Production (eu-west-1)`.
- `plugin_id` (String) Which provider plugin this account is for, e.g. `aws`. Resolve the valid ids with `data.infrawrench_plugins`. Fixed at creation: an account is its credential, and a credential does not change provider.

### Optional

- `bastion_id` (String) Route this account's cloud API traffic through an `infrawrench_bastion`. Omit it to reach the provider directly from Infrawrench.
- `products` (Set of String) The apps this connection is for: any of `infrastructure`, `costs`, `observability`, `incidents`, `security`, `delivery`, `automation` that the plugin offers. Omit it for every app, which is what an account connected before this choice existed has.

Collection follows the choice, so the credential only needs the permissions of the apps listed: an account for `["costs"]` alone has its bill read and no resources synced, and one without `costs` has no cost data collected. A plugin offers the apps its capabilities power (most clouds offer `infrastructure`, `costs` and `observability`); naming one it does not offer, or setting this on a plugin that offers no choice, is rejected when applied with a message listing what it does offer.

Do not list every app the plugin offers: that is the same as omitting the attribute, and it is stored as such. The provider keeps your list in state in that case, so an out-of-band change back to every app is not reported as drift.

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) Server-assigned account id. Use it with `terraform import` — though an imported account has no `credentials` in state, so supply them in configuration.

## Import

Import is supported using the following syntax:

The [`terraform import` command](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/cli/commands/import) can be used, for example:

```shell
# The id is in the URL when you open the object in the app, and in the
# --json output of the Infrawrench CLI.
terraform import infrawrench_account.example 9a8b7c6d-1e2f-3a4b-5c6d-7e8f9a0b1c2d
```
